## Context

This is a scoped follow-up to #1 and the implementation in draft PR #2. The source snapshot is commit `9aff16ceb97e9420ab346552c04405c38d2ffde8`; it is not a claim that the default branch already contains that work. Coordinate the implementation baseline with PR #2 or its merged successor. Issue creation and the ready-for-agent label do not authorize provider launches, trust/permission changes, audit adoption, billing changes or new spending. Follow the execution host’s current policy and preserve existing evidence.

## Triage evidence

- Confirmed static control-flow gap and an existing published deferred finding. No fresh live timing or resistant-child run was claimed by this triage.
- Existing tests deliver input after observing termination and use a fake provider that exits on SIGTERM; they do not cover the indefinitely resistant no-input case.

**Redundancy check:** Inspected provider error handling/input wait/cleanup, the existing post-ready error tests, fixture behavior and context cancellation/release checks. Existing related mechanisms do not satisfy the specific remaining contract below.

**Prior rejection check:** No rejection knowledge base or matching rejection record was present in the inspected checkout. No other follow-up issue existed at triage start.

## Dated source references

- [Provider lifecycle implementation](https://github.com/arduinitavares/the-council/blob/9aff16ceb97e9420ab346552c04405c38d2ffde8/src/pilot/provider-session.ts)
- [Existing lifecycle regression cases](https://github.com/arduinitavares/the-council/blob/9aff16ceb97e9420ab346552c04405c38d2ffde8/test/pilot/provider-session.test.ts)
- [Published deferred no-input finding](https://github.com/arduinitavares/the-council/blob/9aff16ceb97e9420ab346552c04405c38d2ffde8/docs/qualification/gemini-startup-verification.md)
- [Owned context release checks](https://github.com/arduinitavares/the-council/blob/9aff16ceb97e9420ab346552c04405c38d2ffde8/src/pilot/context-driver.ts)

The agent-brief comment is the implementation contract. Parent #1 stays open until its independent operational acceptance criteria are met.

> *This was generated by AI during triage.*

## Agent Brief

**Category:** bug
**State:** ready-for-agent, explicitly requested by the maintainer. This means the specification is ready; dependency or runtime gates are not implied to have passed.
**Summary:** Begin bounded cleanup after provider failure without waiting for input

**Current behavior:**
After a provider becomes ready, a parser/stderr error can request SIGTERM while the session continues waiting for an input file until the assignment deadline if the child remains alive. That input wait does not check the recorded error. Forced cleanup is reached only afterward. With no preceding provider error, a missing input file can surface as an incidental ENOENT. Existing queued-parser barriers prevent late input delivery but do not resolve this wait.

**Desired behavior:**
A terminal pre-input failure immediately exits the input wait into bounded owned cleanup. Missing input at its deadline has a stable explicit outcome. Preserve the first substantive failure, zero delivered-input accounting, cancellation semantics and positive resource-settlement requirements.

**Key interfaces:**

- `runProviderSession()`, `WrapperAssignment.deadline`, the queued `parsing` promise, provider error/readiness/input state and cancellation requests.
- Process settlement reports and `ContextWrapperTransport.cancel()` / `release()` ownership checks.

**Acceptance criteria:**

- [ ] Add a portable offline RED using a fake provider with valid initialization that emits a post-ready terminal error, ignores SIGTERM and keeps its stream open. Supply neither input nor cancellation. Use an independent fixture watchdog and owned cleanup.
- [ ] Compare different future assignment durations: after the fix, pre-input failure must enter cleanup promptly rather than waiting out the remaining assignment lifetime.
- [ ] With controlled time and the full existing allowance, preserve the existing approximately two-second escalation eligibility and at-most-30-second cleanup interval, shortened by any earlier applicable cancellation bound. Do not claim these acceptance limits were measured during triage.
- [ ] Every no-input case records zero calls, no delivered user input and no inference-start receipt. Late input after the error cannot change that.
- [ ] Missing input receives a specific stable deadline/error result; an earlier substantive provider error is not replaced by a filesystem error. Pre-input cancellation cannot become an acknowledged active-turn cancellation.
- [ ] Signals affect only the owned provider group. Closure, process group/observed-descendant settlement, timers and exact wrapper/terminal release remain separately verified. Unknown cleanup must remain unknown, with duplicate-stop protections preserved.

**Out of scope:**

- Duplicate run identifiers, expired requests at entry, provider trust/startup admission, billing and inference-cancellation redesign.
- Diagnostic retention changes or a live provider run solely to reproduce this offline lifecycle bug.

**Execution and delivery:**
Work against a revision containing the relevant PR #2 implementation. Recheck the current tree and host policy. Supply portable offline coverage and a reviewable change or validation record, with fresh independent review of material work. Required live evidence must use already-authorized, qualified routes and finite declared call/deadline limits. If a required external capability or permission is unavailable, retain a precise blocker and leave operational completion open; do not substitute a diagnostics-only result for the requested behavior. No global settings, accounts, historical artifacts or unrelated work may be changed under this brief.


**Dependencies:** No sibling prerequisite. Runtime and authorization gates in the brief still apply.
